The structure of a chlorofluorocarbon polymer is shown.

Displayed polymer structure: –C(CH₃)(H)–C(Cl)(F)–C(CH₃)(H)–C(Cl)(F)–

Which monomer is used to make this polymer?

mx.teacher_note: Only pure substances can be components of a mixture.

intelligence.enrichment: A mixture forms when two or more substances are mixed without a chemical reaction; the individual substances retain their properties and are called components. Physical mixing without chemical change produces a mixture, and retained component properties make the sample behave like its original substances. The learner correctly applies this rule: A mixture forms when two or more substances are mixed without a chemical reaction; the individual substances retain their properties and are called components. A sample is a mixture only when it looks blended into one smooth material.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Elements, compounds and mixtures. The student must decide: Decide whether a sample is a mixture by checking whether two or more substances are physically mixed while each component keeps its own properties. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
